messages.subject: mirt vs. ltm
parts:
Hi all,

Are there any advantages to using mirt rather than ltm when conducting a graded response IRT model?  The fundamental analyses involve item information curves and item characteristic curves.  The only group comparison involved is gender, and both packages can address DIF.  

How is it possible to get different slope (a) and location (b) estimates when using both ltm and mirt?

What are possible reasons for, and fixes for, successfully running a chunk, but when trying to run a single line to see a plot, it doesn't run?

Thank you,

Robert

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: mirt vs. ltm
parts:
This might help:

https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/63891/is-r-output-reliable-specially-irt-package-ltm

And I'm not sure ltm would be the best for DIF analyses (would require ad-hoc equating rather than direct model fitting). DIF testing is generally a multiple-group type approach, which mirt supports via multipleGroup(), with effect size estimates such as DRF(), and automated detection functions like DIF(). It's a free world though, so go with whatever you feel is appropriate.

Phil
